scope: Grounded turning interpretation of the spiral surface and mast on Ms B 83v. Human drive is a declared modern presentation assumption. No complete flying vehicle is claimed.
gaps: Historical drive and torque-reaction control unresolved. Complete status applies to grounded rotating object only.
Holder-specific image reuse terms not verified.
Helix pitch, taper and all construction sizes except radius are assumptions.

scale_m.note: Swept radial extent at most 4.6788 m, the rim wire's outer edge at the first rib (every part measured at rest; the turn keeps the radius). Conservative bounds X and Z [-4.75, 4.75], Y [0, 6.1]. The deck and the bearing block stay on the floor; the mast turns from world y=0.19 (its iron pivot) to 6.0, its iron cap reaching 6.018. Starting sail radius 4.6688 m equals 8*0.5836 under the commissioned conversion.

frame.origin: Ground projection of central assembly. Local transforms relative to parent. Ground y=0.

assumptions.statement: r=4.6688m, total mass400kg=4people x75kg +100kg machine, rho=1.225kg/m3, g=9.81m/s2, assumed figure of merit0.65. Alternative diameter5m and one-person100kg cases are sensitivity calculations.
assumptions.reason: Four-person drive is a modern reconstruction hypothesis. None of these mass or efficiency inputs was measured on a Leonardo machine.

assumptions.statement: Assembly placement is fixed in the room. Only the explicit joints move. No whole-machine travel is inferred.
assumptions.reason: Prevents an unfinished study appearing to be a working mechanism.

assumptions.statement: Every numeric dimension, coordinate, orientation, mesh subdivision, tube radius and repeated-element placement in parts is an explicit modern modelling choice except quantities explicitly identified as Leonardo dimensions in the part notes. These values are the complete procedural definition.
assumptions.reason: The folio does not specify fabrication geometry. The model is newly specified from the sheet and never copied from a replica.

assumptions.statement: Every motion limit, pivot, period and rate below is a modern demonstration assumption unless a source is named. All fixed children follow their parent rigidly.
assumptions.reason: No historical operating rate is measured.

assumptions.statement: The mast stands in an oak bearing block on the platform: its turned foot runs in an iron-lined hole at the top of the block and its iron pivot on an iron step at the bottom, 0.6 m apart. A frame of eight oak legs turns with the mast, from an oak crown wedged on the mast at 2.24 to 2.35 m down to a foot ring of eight felloes 1.55 m out, 0.38 to 0.46 m over the floor; four push bars are shipped into an oak head at 1.05 m, pinned, and run on through every second leg. The spiral starts at 2.5 m, so the bars, the frame and the people who walk the bars stay under the cloth. Rib roots are set 12 mm into the mast.
assumptions.reason: The sheet draws a cone of members from a round base up to the spiral; how it is made, that it turns, and the drive are C choices, so the drive four people walk on the deck holds the bars and the mast upright.

[folio] Linen with its pores stopped with starch, eight braccia from the rim to the centre (4.6688 m), drawn on 83v as a flat spiral of about two whorls, the upper narrower. [geometry] Two turns from 2.5 m to 5.0 m over the floor, the rim falling from 4.6688 m to 2.9 m: the turns, the rise of 1.25 m a turn and the end radius are read off the drawing's proportions, the metres are the museum's. The spiral winds so that the turn the mast is given drives the air down. The cloth is sewn from radial panels no wider than 62 cm at the rim, doubled into a hem round the iron wire and a band at the mast, and hangs up to 1.2 per cent of its span between the ribs. The listed vertices sample the surface coarsely; the helicoid entry is its full definition.

joints.notes: Mast turns about the vertical axis in its bearing block: the turned foot in the iron-lined hole of the block, the iron pivot on the iron step. q is an unwrapped angle. The bearing and the human bars are explicitly assumed.

drive.justification: A slow ground demonstration. No historical speed supplied. This speed is not asserted to generate flight.

joint_values.spin: q(t)=pi*t/6 radians, t=phase-local seconds. Across repeats add2*pi each cycle.

motion.visitor_12s: One full turn. The platform stays on the ground.

animation_notes: No undocumented flight, lift, bounce, mechanism or invisible reset.
No vertical translation. Do not describe5rpm as takeoff speed.
Continuous angles must not jump backward at loop boundaries.
The fixed ground installation supplies reaction torque. It is not a solution for airborne torque balance.
The push bars turn at 1.05 m inside the frame, whose crown stays under 2.35 m; the cloth and its canes start above 2.45 m. The spiral winds so that the given turn drives the air down.

sheet_vs_reconstruction: The text specifies an iron outer rim, cane framework, sealed linen and a small paper model driven by a twisted iron strip [s-folio].
Soldatini and Somenzi, 1952 to 1953, added a four-person drive. Their own museum now warns that this may exceed the sheet. A Guidonia model dates 1938 [s-model,s-guidonia].

[folio] The sheet draws a flat spiral of about two whorls high on a mast, over a cone of members and a round base; its note asks for linen stopped with starch, long thick canes and an iron wire rim as thick as a cord. [geometry] The two turns, the rise and the taper follow the drawing's proportions; the frame's legs, crown and foot ring, the canes' splices and lashings, the seams, the bearing block, the drive and the deck are the museum's reconstruction of how a workshop of the period would build that, and the spiral is wound so the turn it is given would drive the air down [a-geometry,a-motion].

dimensions.quote: dal cerchio al centro sia braccia 8
dimensions.conversion: Literal radius 8 x 0.5836 m=4.6688 m. Diameter 9.3376 m. Milan work location does not establish the unit. The commissioned Florentine braccio is explicit. Museum IGB 6 instead describes 8 Florentine braccia as a base of about 5 m, without resolving radius versus diameter [s-folio,s-model].

claims.claimed: Rapidly turned sealed linen screw would rise. Small spring paper model proposed [s-folio].
claims.tested: No completed experiment or measured thrust is recorded in the inspected passage [s-folio].
claims.built_lifetime: No securely documented lifetime build or flight located.
claims.later: Prete 2022 tested 0.152 m rotors and a powered quadrotor. Crimson Spin used four electric rotor units. Neither validates a human-driven full-scale machine [s-rotor,s-drone].

physics.formula: Ideal actuator disk: A=pi*r^2, T=mg, vi=sqrt(T/(2*rho*A)), Pideal=T*vi. Assumed shaft power=Pideal/0.65.
physics.inputs: All mass, density, gravity and efficiency values are a-physics. Physiology is s-human.
physics.results: r 4.6688 m gives A 68.479 m 2. At 400 kg T 3924 N, vi 4.836 m/s, Pideal 18.98 kW, assumed shaft 29.20 kW. Four exceptional one-hour riders at 509.5 W yield 2.038 kW before transmission losses. At diameter 5 m, Pideal 35.44 kW. At 100 kg total and literal radius, Pideal 2.372 kW versus 0.5095 kW elite one-hour benchmark.
physics.limitations: This is a favourable lower bound for an ideal disk, not a prediction of the screw thrust at 5 rpm. Swirl, profile drag, structure and anti-torque requirements increase demand. A low-friction grounded exhibit can turn without hovering.
physics.verdict_en: Even an ideal 400 kg version needs about 19 kW to hover, far beyond four elite riders.
physics.verdict_de: Schon das ideale 400 kg-Modell braucht rund 19 kW zum Schweben, weit mehr als vier Spitzenradfahrer leisten.

myths.earliest_located: An explicit dated modern example located is the 2022 University of Maryland presentation calling it a proto-helicopter. The 1938 Guidonia object documents earlier reconstruction, not the first claim. Historical first claimant remains unverified [s-drone,s-guidonia].
myths.correction: A rotating lift proposal and an electric quadrotor are not a demonstrated Renaissance helicopter.

research.confidence: High folio and wording. Conditional dimensions. Low historical drive, power and completed build certainty.

geometry_validation.method: Local primitive and mesh geometry transformed through the specified joint hierarchy. Forty-nine poses across 12 seconds, or one static pose. Tube centreline bounds conservatively expanded by radius. Analytic motion extrema and attachment clearances are given in animation_notes.
geometry_validation.result: All tested swept points are inside the declared conservative bounding box. Geometry defines a C exhibit interpretation, not structural certification.
